sentences.zh: 道古在鄂州日，以貪暴聞，懼終得罪，乃薦山人柳泌以媚於上。

translations.literal: In Daogu's days at E Prefecture, he was known for greed and violence; fearing he would ultimately incur guilt, he recommended the mountain recluse Liu Bi to flatter the emperor.
translations.idiomatic: While at E Prefecture Li Daogu had a reputation for greed and cruelty. Fearing eventual disgrace, he recommended the mountaintop recluse Liu Bi to curry favor with the emperor.

sentences.zh: 後又為左金吾衛將軍。

translations.literal: Later he also served as general of the Left Jinwu Guard.
translations.idiomatic: He later served as general of the Left Jinwu Guard.

sentences.zh: 憲宗季年頗信方士，銳於服食，詔天下搜訪奇士。

translations.literal: In Xianzong's late years he greatly trusted alchemical masters, was keen on ingesting elixirs; he decreed searching the empire for extraordinary men.
translations.idiomatic: In his later years Emperor Xianzong placed great faith in alchemists and eagerly pursued elixirs of immortality. He ordered an empire-wide search for wonder-workers.

sentences.zh: 宰相皇甫鎛方諛媚固寵，道古言柳泌有道術，鎛得進之，待詔翰林。

translations.literal: Chief minister Huangfu Bo was then flattering to secure favor; Daogu said Liu Bi possessed the Way and its arts; Bo was able to present him, and he awaited edicts at the Hanlin Academy.
translations.idiomatic: Chief Minister Huangfu Bo was then currying favor through flattery. Daogu claimed that Liu Bi possessed Daoist arts. Bo presented him to the throne, and Liu was retained at the Hanlin Academy.

sentences.zh: 憲宗服餌過當，暴成狂躁之疾，以至棄代。

translations.literal: Xianzong took elixirs in excess and suddenly developed a disorder of frenzy and agitation, until he abandoned the throne.
translations.idiomatic: Emperor Xianzong took elixirs in excess and suddenly fell into violent mania, which led to his death.

sentences.zh: 穆宗在東宮，扼腕於其事，及居喪，皆竄逐誅之。

translations.literal: Muzong, while in the Eastern Palace, wrung his hands over this affair; when he assumed mourning, he banished and executed them all.
translations.idiomatic: While still heir apparent, Muzong had been deeply troubled by these events. Once he assumed the throne in mourning, he banished and executed all those involved.

sentences.zh: 鎛既貶責，授道古循州司馬，終以服丹藥，歐血而卒。

translations.literal: After Bo was demoted and censured, Daogu was appointed acting chief secretary of Xunzhou; in the end, because he had taken elixir drugs, he vomited blood and died.
translations.idiomatic: After Bo was demoted and punished, Daogu was appointed acting chief secretary of Xun Prefecture. He ultimately died vomiting blood from the elixirs he had taken.

sentences.zh: 【史贊】

translations.literal: Historian's Commendation
translations.idiomatic: Historian's Commendation

sentences.zh: 史臣曰：李勉、李皋，稟性端莊，處身廉潔，臨民蒞事，動有美聲，可謂宗臣之英也。

translations.literal: The historiographer states: Li Mian and Li Gao received upright and dignified natures, conducted themselves with incorruptible purity, and in governing the people and handling affairs always won fine repute—they may be called the finest among imperial clansmen.
translations.idiomatic: The historiographer writes: Li Mian and Li Gao were upright and dignified by nature, lived with incorruptible integrity, and in governing the people and conducting affairs always earned praise. They may truly be called the finest of the imperial clan.

sentences.zh: 若夫治軍旅，禦寇戎，謀必臧，戰必勝，則又勉不及皋遠矣。

translations.literal: As for governing armies, repelling border enemies, plans always proving sound and battles always won, in this Mian fell far short of Gao.
translations.idiomatic: In raising armies, repelling invaders, and achieving unfailing strategy and victory in battle, however, Mian fell far short of Gao.

sentences.zh: 道古便佞，奸以事君，何父子之不相類也。

translations.literal: Daogu was fawning and crafty, serving his lord with treachery—how unlike father and son!
translations.idiomatic: Daogu was sycophantic and treacherous in his service to the throne. How unlike father and son the two generations were!

sentences.zh: 贊曰：我宗之英，曰皋與勉，才雖不同，道豈相遠。

translations.literal: The commendation states: The finest of our clan are called Gao and Mian; though their talents differ, how could their Way be far apart?
translations.idiomatic: The commendation reads: The finest of our house are Gao and Mian. Their talents differed, yet how far apart could their moral way have been?
